operations.comment: ; Fixed CPU views of immutable PRG tables. PRG remains fixed under CNROM.
; Biased aliases are indexed bases; the first accessed element may lie later.
; CPU $8000-$BFFF is fixed PRG on this CNROM image. Physical PRG banks 0/1
; occupy those two 8 KiB slots; the upper two slots hold fixed data banks 2/3.
; RAM arrays use parallel per-slot fields. Explicit a:/z: widths preserve encoding.
; Immediate values are byte-sized selectors unless a nearby comment gives units.
; iNES header: 32 KiB PRG, 32 KiB CHR, CNROM mapper 3 and vertical mirroring. Header/trainer offsets
; are physical file identities; this image has no trainer.
; Disable interrupts, initialize the stack and wait for two vblanks before warm-start initialization.
; CNROM keeps this PRG window fixed; CHR selection is separate.
; Limit a vblank batch to nine eight-byte queue records. Each record supplies a nametable address,
; metatile index and attribute mask/value.
; Write the four tile quadrants and merge the affected palette attribute bits. Queue indices advance
; in eight-byte records.
; Continue the metatile batch until the queue is empty or nine records have been written.
; Restore PPU shadows, sample controllers and service sound/music before restoring interrupted
; registers.
; Read controllers and advance both audio engines before the interrupt epilogue.
; The IRQ vector points directly to this RTI; ordinary NMI reaches it after restoring registers.
; Rejoin the bounded queued-metatile writer.
; Save registers, DMA page $07 to OAM and reapply the CHR bank. Frame counters control scrolling; a
; synthetic RTS dispatch selects one of eight background-update phases.
; Decrement vertical scroll; only even positions dispatch a staged background-update phase.
; Advance the fifteen-row counter. At a new row select the next compressed map pointer or interpret
; stage-stream commands.
; Advance the stage stream until a row pointer is selected. $E0 and $F0 command families change scroll
; cadence and stage/substage markers.
; Discard the synthetic dispatch return, restore PPU shadows and decode the next row before servicing
; input/audio.
; Expand stream tokens into sixteen metatile indices. Derive nametable and attribute addresses from
; vertical scroll for later staged PPU writes.
; Literal tokens emit one metatile; higher token families spawn objects, translate through tables, or
; repeat the following value. $EF ends the row.
; Restore PPUMASK, scroll and PPUCTRL from RAM shadows; two PPUADDR writes reset the address before
; scrolling.
; Resolve sixteen metatiles into four parallel tile rows and palette selectors. The level pointers
; select the current landscape's graphics tables.
; Write sixteen pairs of bottom tile quadrants to the prepared nametable row.
; Read eight existing attribute bytes, then merge sixteen metatile palettes into the appropriate
; quadrants, preserving the other row.
; Two attribute-quadrant preservation masks used by MergeAttributeRow; the complementary quadrant
; receives the new palette bits.
; Write sixteen pairs of top tile quadrants to the prepared nametable row.
; Upload the eight merged palette attribute bytes.
; Set the PPU address from high byte A and low byte X; caller must have reset the PPU latch.
; Disable rendering/NMI, initialize palette and scroll state, hide sprites and clear both nametables.
; Fill $800 bytes of nametable memory with zero, with rendering disabled.
; A nonzero request selects a background palette; negative requests cycle selection using the frame
; counter.
; A selects one sixteen-byte background palette.
; Write the default background and sprite palette blocks, then reset PPU addressing.
; X selects a sixteen-byte sprite palette block.
; Wait for vblank to become set, then read until it clears. The PPUSTATUS reads also reset the
; address/scroll latch.
; Synchronize to vblank, clear rendering bits and disable NMI through the RAM shadows.
; Hide sprites, synchronize to vblank, upload scroll/OAM and enable NMI and rendering.
; Strobe both standard controllers and collect eight serial bits each. Either low input bit counts as
; pressed.
; Fold the sampled controller bit into X; Y counts the remaining serial reads.
; Eight sixteen-byte palette blocks followed by eight little-endian return-minus-one background-update
; targets. BackgroundPaletteBiasedBase deliberately points sixteen bytes before the first palette so
; indexed selectors choose the intended block. The NMI dispatcher pushes high then low bytes and
; enters through RTS.
; Two signature bytes distinguish a warm reset. A cold reset clears all eight RAM pages before
; recording the signature.
; Clear update queue and scroll enable, then reset object state.
; Select one of four demonstration stage selectors and mark attract input active.
; Keep the attract flag from A and join common game initialization.
; Clear the stage selector and attract flag, then initialize lives, movement and weapon defaults.
; Load stage-specific stream, landscape and boss/exploration selectors; reset player and object state
; before entering the frame loop.
; Update player, projectiles, objects, bosses, HUD and sprites once per NMI. Death, stage completion,
; pause and attract exit leave this loop.
; Normal play tests Start; attract mode also tests Select before considering the death state.
; Attract death returns to reset. Normal play clears shots, waits through death presentation and
; reduces power/lives before restarting or offering continue.
; Suspend scrolling and toggle audio pause state. Require Start release, a fresh press and another
; release before resuming.
; Run the boss defeat transition effect and advance to the next stage selector.
; Advance through fourteen exploration/boss selectors; wrap to the first stage and increment the
; completed-loop counter.
; Check stream completion and player position after scroll changes. Carry reports a stage transition;
; attract movement may be adjusted near the boundary.
; Wait for the next NMI, clear OAM and run the sprite presentation pipeline.
; Compose player, boss, object, projectile and HUD sprites into the current OAM buffer.
; Wait for NMI to advance its counter, then alternate OAM allocation order with bit $40.
; Hide all sixty-four sprites by setting Y=$F8, and reset the OAM allocator.
; Refresh score state; a pending extra-life notification requests its sound once.
; Request the extra-life sound using the common forced-priority path.
; Clear the rolling metatile collision map, preserving element zero.
; Clear the eight score digits and extra-life bookkeeping.
; Disable DMC and APU channels and clear pending sound/music/pause requests; disable the APU frame IRQ.
; Select stage palettes and tile/collision tables, then decode and upload fifteen metatile rows with
; rendering off.
; Landscape pointer sets plus parallel fourteen-entry stage tables. StageSelector indexes
; exploration/boss kind, substage, scroll enable, boss ID, palettes, row stream start/end, landscape
; and music. Four-entry attract tables choose shorter demonstration routes. Pointer groups select
; metatile quadrants, palette, collision and replacement tables; PRG addresses remain fixed under
; CNROM.
; Consume the pending pickup kind. Effects include speed, weapon, health, temporary transformation and
; clearing enemy states; limits are enforced here.
; Eight encoded score awards used after the bounded pickup progression index; high nibble selects
; decimal position and low nibble supplies the increment.
; Restore base speed and clear weapon, accessory and pickup progression.
; Handle exit/death states, terrain hazards, damage, recovery timers, scrolling displacement and
; controller movement.
; Request exit audio, reset player powerups and start the player exit countdown.
; When the background advances, test the player's feet against the collision map. Solid terrain pushes
; the player toward the lower edge; overflow begins death recovery.
; Resolve directional movement against terrain and screen bounds. Jump timing can preserve direction
; across a gap; B drives repeated shots and A starts a new jump on a press edge.
; Use the weapon-specific repeat interval and available slot count. Initialize a projectile from the
; player's position and request the matching shot sound.
; Highest allocatable player-shot slot for each of the four weapon levels; the firing allocator
; searches downward from this value.
; Convert the player's foot position to a metatile and compare landscape-specific hazard IDs. Returns
; comparison flags used by the player state handler.
; Four sound IDs selected by weapon level when a normal shot is allocated.
; Test the collision bitset. Pickup metatiles trigger a pickup request and replace the metatile;
; jumping bypasses selected obstacles.
; Compare the player rectangle against eight active objects and six enemy projectiles. Set the hit
; flag and retire colliding projectile entries.
; Combine both controllers during play; attract mode substitutes the scripted directional sequence and
; holds fire.
; Update facing from A only on every fourth animation frame.
; Advance six projectile slots. Weapon kinds select straight, curved or spread motion; terrain
; collisions can transform destructible metatiles and spawn their contents.
; Four signed horizontal steps for spread projectiles, indexed by their saved phase.
; Render normal shot tiles or temporarily substitute player state to draw transformed projectiles with
; the player renderer.
; Copy the collision probe's cell coordinates to the object spawn coordinates.
; Parallel projectile animation frame and mirror tables. Shot kind and frame phase select the entry;
; the renderer consumes frame and flip separately.
; Draw the paired accessory sprites, selecting animation and jump offsets from player state.
; Map pixel coordinates to a rolling metatile cell, load its ID and test the corresponding bit in the
; landscape collision bitset. Returns zero for passable cells.
; Spawn a map object, then update the collision cell while preserving X and Y.
; Replace the collision-map cell at the current pixel probe with A.
; Combine vertical screen position with scrolling, wrap the fifteen-row ring and return the packed
; row/column cell index in Y.
; Eight one-bit collision masks followed by sixteen signed player jump-height offsets.
; ProbeCollisionMap uses the former; player and accessory renderers use the latter.
; Select normal, transformed, hurt or death frames. Jump offsets and terrain priority affect sprite
; positions and attributes.
; Emit two player tiles, then move the drawing origin to the next row.
; Resolve a player tile and flip flag from the normal frame table, then submit it to OAM.
; Resolve transformed-player tiles from the larger frame table and share the OAM emission path.
; Draw the larger player form as three rows of three tiles with facing-dependent mirroring.
; Emit three tiles and advance the drawing origin to the next row.
; Append Y, tile, attributes and X from the sprite scratch variables to page $07. Skip tile zero and
; stop when the byte allocator wraps.
; Facing-to-frame bases, walk-phase offsets and packed player tile layouts. Normal frames use six
; tiles; transformed frames use a larger layout. Tile bit seven supplies a mirror flag and tile zero
; is transparent. Jump offsets are applied by the renderer rather than encoded in these layouts.
; Allocate one of twenty pending map-object records from an encoded stream token. Store cell, kind and
; descriptor-table parameters while preserving the stream cursor.
; Parallel map-animation initialization tables: lifetime seed, frame interval and kind/variant state
; seeds. These are indexed by the high/low nibbles of compressed-row object tokens. Array subdivisions
; follow the consumers in SpawnStreamObject.
; Advance twenty map animation records and expire them according to scrolling speed. The record arrays
; hold cell coordinates, animation kind, phase, hold count and frame interval.
; Each active record advances through a bounded frame range. Zero records supply delay values; other
; frames stamp rectangular metatile patterns and update the collision map through the queue.
; Select an eight-cell pattern and advance the animation cell vertically, wrapping the fifteen-row
; collision ring.
; Stamp eight metatiles with the row break after four cells; preserve the caller's animation record
; through scratch state.
; Stamp a ten-cell pattern, then move its origin horizontally and reverse direction at the two limits.
; Request a sound at the two distinguished animation frames.
; Back up the column and advance the cell row for the next pattern line.
; Back up two columns and advance one row; return the new row for ring wrapping.
; Map-animation frame ranges and six/eight/ten-cell stamp scripts. Nonzero records provide metatiles
; to spawn/update; zero-leading records select variant-dependent delays. Stamp helpers specify row
; breaks and fifteen-row ring wrapping. Exact game names for every animated structure remain
; unresolved.
; Build an eight-byte PPU update record and append it to the page-$06 ring, waiting for NMI when the
; queue is full. Preserve X/Y.
; Convert cell coordinates and metatile A to nametable address and attribute quadrant mask/value. The
; caller copies the prepared eight bytes to the update queue.
; Decode a stream wave token into count and spawn interval. The row cursor determines the initial
; horizontal position.
; Y selects count/interval entries. Initialize the wave timer and set the spawn column from the
; compressed-row output cursor.
; Advance the wave timer and allocate one of eight enemy slots. Initialization uses the same return-
; minus-one handler table as movement; carry distinguishes initialization from update.
; Clear all eight enemy kind/state entries, then clear player shots, enemy shots and map animation
; records.
; Clear six player/enemy projectile entries and twenty map animation records.
; Process eight slots. High states animate death or knockback; normal states dispatch by kind, check
; player-shot damage, award points and periodically fire. Preserve the previous player position for
; follower motion.
; After a kind-specific update, test player shots and apply damage thresholds. Loop count increases
; enemy durability and firing frequency; transformed attacks award extra score.
; Eight signed horizontal knockback steps for the high enemy-state family, indexed by saved pose.
; Compare six active player shots with the rectangle origin in scratch. Transformed shots use larger
; bounds. Carry reports a hit; most normal shots are consumed. Preserve X/Y.
; Move an enemy down only when scroll changes; retire it below the lower bound.
; Clear this slot's state; the other parallel fields are initialized on next allocation.
; On initialization place the enemy opposite the player. Later updates weave horizontally and descend,
; retiring below the screen.
; Use a sixteen-frame phase clock, then share horizontal waveform movement.
; Use a four-frame phase clock. A sixteen-sample table supplies horizontal displacement; a direction
; bit reverses each cycle.
; Use object coordinates and direction to draw the two-frame animation.
; Draw the two-frame family beginning at frame six.
; Draw the two-frame family beginning at frame four, with direction-dependent flip.
; Return the low animation bit from the global frame counter, with carry clear for frame-base addition.
; Initialize a delay phase, then alternate scrolling wait and a timed leap. The leap uses a vertical
; waveform and reverses horizontal travel halfway through.
; Hide the waiting phase; select leap frames and facing from the leap timer.
; Initialize from the opposite side, then descend while accelerating horizontally.
; Apply signed horizontal speed, incrementing speed every thirty-two frames.
; Initialize opposite the player, animate six poses, and combine slow horizontal weaving with a
; vertical waveform.
; Resolve flip and frame from the six-pose lookup tables.
; Six mirror flags followed by six animation frame IDs; shared by the wave/fast-descending enemy draw
; handlers.
; Advance a six-pose animation every fourth frame and wrap at six.
; Initialization needs no work. Descend every other frame and retire at the lower bound.
; Resolve one of four frames using the shared animation phase.
; Four animation frame IDs for the slow descending enemy.
; Return bits two and three of the global frame counter as a four-frame selector in Y.
; Initialize a delay; while active follow scrolling and cycle a seven-bit action timer.
; Choose the horizontal flip from player-relative position, then select one of two timer-dependent
; poses.
; The phase bit alternates downward motion and half-speed upward motion; retire below the screen.
; Select a four-frame animation from the shared frame clock.
; Four animation frames for the bobbing enemy family, indexed by the shared four-frame clock.
; Initialize opposite the player, then combine a faster horizontal phase with the vertical waveform
; and six-pose animation.
; Follow scrolling and approach the player horizontally once every eight frames.
; Select the tracking enemy's four-frame animation.
; Four animation frames for the slow player-tracking enemy.
; Delay entry, follow scrolling, then open and close through timed poses. The exposed phase raises the
; firing timer to its minimum.
; Draw only when the emergence state supplies a nonzero pose.
; Wait through negative timer states, follow scrolling, and intermittently move toward the player only
; if the candidate cell is passable.
; Use a waiting pose for negative states, otherwise animate four poses.
; Four animation frames for the terrain-aware tracking enemy. Its negative waiting state uses a
; separate fixed pose.
; Initialization captures absolute player-relative deltas and an octant. Updates use an error
; accumulator to approximate a line toward that captured point; retire outside screen bounds.
; Capture player-relative absolute deltas and an octant/dominant-axis selector for subsequent integer
; line motion.
; Copy eight signed unit steps into shared scratch, then advance along the captured aim vector.
; Apply a signed step on the major axis and accumulated error on the minor axis. Retire the slot at
; screen bounds.
; Eight signed unit steps used by the aimed-enemy integer line algorithm. Different octants index
; overlapping halves of this table.
; Draw a two-frame aimed enemy animation.
; Choose a pseudo-random aligned column on initialization, then descend three pixels per update.
; Return immediately while the fast descender remains within bounds.
; Use the six-pose animation and flip tables.
; Six frame IDs paired with the common six-pose flip table for the fast descender.
; Initialize below the player, then copy the player's movement delta into this object while
; maintaining its own action state.
; Compute the follower's right-hand arc position from radius and phase speed.
; Compute the corresponding left-hand arc position.
; Draw the follower frame at its current position.
; Initialize on the side opposite the player at a fixed height, then cross horizontally while applying
; a vertical waveform.
; Descend for a fixed introduction, wait while following the scroll, then capture an aim line and move
; along it.
; Use a fixed introductory pose and a two-frame active animation.
; Eight signed three-pixel unit steps for the delayed aimed-enemy family.
; Choose an aligned random column, capture the player-relative aim vector, then share the error-
; accumulating movement implementation.
; Load this movement family's signed unit-step table and share the aimed line update.
; Render the fixed aimed-enemy frame.
; Eight signed four-pixel unit steps for the random-column aimed-enemy family.
; Descend until reaching the player's height, curve toward the player with paired waveforms, then exit
; horizontally.
; Resolve the four-frame animation for the turning movement family.
; Four animation frames for the turning enemy.
; Initialize at the lower screen edge and weave upward using the negated vertical waveform.
; Convert the current drawing position to the shared nine-slot shadow list.
; Mix the random state, monotonically incremented counter and frame count. The returned accumulator is
; used for spawn columns and intermittent behavior.
; Allocate one of six enemy shots and capture the player-relative absolute deltas and dominant-axis
; octant. Motion later follows this captured line rather than continuously homing.
; Step six shots using integer error accumulation on the minor axis and signed unit movement on the
; major axis. Zero Y marks an unused slot.
; Eight signed unit steps for enemy shots. Octant and major-axis selection intentionally use biased
; indexed bases; these are displacements, not code pointers.
; Submit one tile per active enemy shot using the shared OAM allocator.
; Dispatch normal enemy sprite handlers by kind; death and knockback states use shared frame families.
; Dispatch pointers store target minus one for RTS entry.
; Prepare the object position and choose one of four death frames.
; A selects a two-by-two tile frame. Attribute and flip tables supply palette and orientation; skip
; zero tiles and preserve the caller's X slot.
; Emit the pair of tiles in one row using the shared tile/attribute resolver.
; Resolve tile and flip-dependent attributes, emit a sprite and advance the horizontal origin eight
; pixels.
; Two-by-two object tile layouts, palette/flip attributes, return-minus-one draw/update handler
; directories, signed movement waves and parallel spawn/score/fire/damage parameters. Enemy kind
; indexes the handler directories; initialization enters movement with carry set and updates with
; carry clear. Individual species names remain unresolved, so handlers use movement mechanics.
; Synchronize a frame and compose player, shadows, radial effect and HUD during the stage transition.
; Initialize eight effect objects around the boss center, with staggered directions and animation
; timers.
; Move effect particles using direction tables, animate and periodically reset them to the center. A
; reset requests the effect sound.
; Place a particle eight pixels above/left of the boss center and start its frame sequence.
; Signed radial-effect movement steps. Direction indices span two overlapping tables, with the Y view
; beginning four bytes after the X view.
; Select one of two frames from the NMI clock.
; Select a two-state mirror flag and draw the fixed frame family.
; Initialization returns immediately; subsequent updates reuse three-pixel downward movement.
; Capture the player-relative aim vector at initialization and use the shared aimed-movement path on
; later updates.
; For the vulnerable boss phase, sum damage from four collision proxy slots, request the hit sound and
; reduce boss HP. Zero HP awards points and marks the boss defeated.
; Position four enemy-like hit rectangles relative to the boss center. Reset damage accumulators
; before player shots are tested.
; Four signed X/Y collision-proxy coordinate pairs relative to the boss center.
; Alternate spawn side and select an enemy kind from the boss-kind table; reuse the ordinary enemy
; allocation/initialization contract.
; Eight enemy kinds indexed by boss kind plus alternating spawn side; the boss dispatcher supplies the
; bias.
; Check damage, then dispatch the boss-kind/state handler. BossState combines a low kind with phase
; flags; defeated and inactive states do no movement.
; Split low/high return-minus-one movement targets for later boss phases. The indexed base includes
; adjacent code bytes; valid kind selectors access this bounded table.
; Enter from above, then weave in both axes and periodically spawn enemies.
; Enter its active phase, cycle firing poses, then bounce within horizontal/vertical bounds for a
; timed interval.
; Run the appearance delay, expose timed poses, then cycle through a table of sixteen spawn positions.
; Sixteen absolute X/Y coordinate pairs. The appearance handler masks its byte index with $1E and
; loads adjacent coordinate bytes; this does not describe natural reachability of every pair.
; Sweep horizontally, reverse at the edges and apply a vertical waveform. A central crossing can
; toggle the mirrored phase and trigger a sound.
; Advance the pose timer and decrease the pose count at fixed intervals.
; Use the action timer and pose count to set or clear the sprite-hidden flag.
; Signed boss movement waveforms: sixteen samples for paired-axis weaving and eight for the vertical
; sweep.
; Set the active phase bit, unhide the boss and reset both action timers.
; Clear the shared action and phase counters.
; Toggle the low pose bit on an eleven-frame interval.
; Advance attack poses on a twenty-one-frame interval and pulse vertical scroll with the attack sound.
; Count down to the next boss enemy spawn, then reload the boss-specific interval.
; Initialize kind-specific position, spawn cadence and HP. The pose starts hidden until the entrance
; handler exposes it.
; Parallel boss initial Y, spawn interval and hit-point tables. Boss kind zero is a no-boss sentinel;
; valid kinds one through four use biased indexed bases.
; Skip inactive, defeated or hidden bosses; otherwise dispatch the kind-specific composition of sprite
; records.
; Compose animated upper and lower records, temporarily substituting the secondary Y coordinate.
; Compose the body and alternating secondary record at the secondary Y coordinate.
; Compose body, attack pose and a fixed secondary component using palette three.
; Compose the body and slow alternating component with the secondary vertical offset.
; Four split low/high return-minus-one draw-handler targets. Boss IDs one through four select each
; byte pair. These bytes are dispatch data, including the formerly rejected false instruction
; candidate.
; A selects a pointer to a variable-width rectangular record: width, height, signed X/Y offsets, then
; row-major tile bytes. Tile sign supplies horizontal flip; zero tiles are transparent and offscreen
; rows are skipped.
; Pointer directory followed by rectangular boss sprite records: width, height, signed X/Y offsets,
; then width times height row-major tile bytes. Zero tile is transparent; bit seven selects horizontal
; flip before the renderer forces the boss tile page. The source renderer checks bottom clipping and
; OAM capacity.
; Clear all nine shadow-list occupancy flags.
; Draw paired mirrored shadow tiles for occupied entries on passable terrain, stopping when OAM fills.
; Append the supplied shadow position to the first free slot; silently drop it when all nine slots are
; occupied.
; Draw remaining lives, significant score digits and health icons. Stop safely if the OAM buffer is
; full.
; Advance the sprite cursor one eight-pixel tile.
; Append a sprite and return nonzero while OAM capacity remains.
; Interpret the high nibble as a decimal digit position and the low nibble as points to add. Attract
; mode suppresses scoring; preserve X/Y.
; Propagate decimal carry toward the more significant digits. Overflow saturates the displayed score
; and high score.
; Compare score against successive thresholds, award extra lives and update the six-digit high score
; lexicographically. Attract mode leaves scores unchanged.
; Set the one-shot sound notification and share the capped life increment.
; Increase lives up to ten and advance the awarded-life threshold index.
; Four four-digit decimal score thresholds used to award successive extra lives; digits are compared
; most significant first.
; Reset the stack, draw title/high-score presentation and wait for a fresh Start press. Timeout starts
; the attract demonstration.
; Present the score/continue screen and wait for Start or timeout. Start plus a direction accepts
; continue; Start alone returns to title.
; Show lives and stage/substage numerals with rendering off, then enable the completed screen.
; Disable rendering, reset scrolling, select the text CHR bank, hide sprites, silence audio and clear
; nametables.
; Draw the shared script used by presentation screens.
; Return only newly pressed controller-one bits and remember the previous held state.
; Set the script pointer from Y:A and interpret PPU-addressed text commands with rendering disabled.
; A record begins with PPU high/low address. Zero ends the script; token zero starts another record,
; one writes zero runs, small tokens write incrementing tiles and larger controls repeat a tile.
; Draw the persistent decimal digits, suppressing leading zeroes and placing the two score rows at
; fixed nametable locations.
; Use Y as the first score-row address and draw the high-score/current-score digit block.
; Scan digits until the first nonzero or row limit, then write the significant digit suffix.
; Store the requested CHR bank shadow, then perform a CNROM write using a ROM byte equal to the bank
; value to tolerate bus conflicts.
; Reapply the selected CHR bank. PRG banks remain fixed; this write only selects the pattern bank.
; CNROM bus-conflict-safe bank bytes, PPU screen command streams, decimal/text tiles, sound
; priorities, forty-four effect dispatch pointers, per-effect channel hold times and APU presets.
; Screen scripts start with PPU address bytes; zero ends a record/script, one emits zero runs, two
; through seven emit ascending tiles, and higher control tokens repeat a tile. See DrawScreenScript
; and UpdateSoundEffects for exact control distinctions. Embedded strings and presets remain local ROM
; assets.
; Accept sound IDs below twenty-two, preserving a higher-priority pending request according to the
; priority table. Preserve X/Y.
; Accept a bounded sound ID and reset the active priority so this request can replace the current
; effect.
; Decrement four music-channel suppression timers, consume a pending effect and initialize its channel
; masks. Dispatch a bounded even selector through forty-four return-minus-one pointers: initialization
; and update entry for each effect.
; Count down the effect lifetime; zero clears its priority and lock state.
; Clear the active effect selector and effect lock; music can regain the affected channels.
; Reset effect/channel timers and silence triangle/noise, then enable the four ordinary APU channels.
; Initialize a three-step pulse preset sequence.
; Advance the preset selector when its delay expires.
; Three pulse preset offsets for the descending three-note effect sequence.
; Start a pulse preset for fourteen effect frames.
; Start the first pulse preset and switch waveform/sweep after its delay.
; Use one additional pulse configuration, then finish.
; Write second-pulse duty/volume and sweep from A/X.
; Tail-call common effect termination after the second phase.
; Initialize four ascending/descending noise-period sweeps.
; Walk the noise period between zero and seven, reversing direction and counting sweeps.
; Initialize a noise sweep whose period increases until sixteen.
; Write and increment the noise period; finish at the upper limit.
; Initialize a pulse preset and drive triangle pitch from its channel suppression timer.
; Lock the effect and initialize four five-frame noise-envelope bursts.
; Retrigger noise length and select volume from the burst-envelope table.
; Six envelope values used by the repeating noise bursts, selected by the five-frame burst countdown.
; Play two noise presets separated by an eight-frame delay and a longer final hold.
; Switch to the final noise preset once, then finish.
; Initialize a five-note pulse sequence with table-driven delays.
; Select the next pulse preset and hold length.
; Tail-call common effect termination after the last selected preset.
; Five pulse preset offsets followed by five hold durations for the five-note effect.
; Initialize a six-step second-pulse pitch sequence.
; Configure sweep and apply the next low timer byte.
; Six low pulse timer bytes for the six-step pitch sequence.
; Load both pulse channels and hold the effect for fifteen frames.
; Load a second-pulse preset for four frames.
; Lock the effect and initialize a three-stage table-driven noise sequence.
; Load noise period, length and hold duration from parallel tables.
; Three noise-period bytes, three length bytes and three hold durations, consumed as parallel arrays.
; Initialize a nine-stage noise sequence.
; Load noise control, period, length and delay from parallel nine-entry tables.
; Four parallel nine-entry arrays: noise control, period, length and step duration.
; Initialize four delayed pulse pitch/sweep steps.
; Advance the pulse timer sequence at four-frame intervals.
; Four low pulse timer bytes for the four-step sweep effect.
; Initialize a multi-phase pulse tone with separate phase and countdown state.
; Alternate timer settings at phase-specific delays, then finish after the third phase.
; Write second-pulse timer low/high from X/A.
; Tail-call effect termination; the following handler initializes a separate two-note sequence.
; Initialize a two-note pulse sequence with six-frame holds.
; Load the next preset when its delay expires.
; Two pulse preset offsets for the two-note sound sequence.
; Lock the effect and initialize four table-selected presets/durations.
; Load the next pulse preset with a twelve-byte register span.
; Four pulse preset offsets followed by four durations for the locked four-note effect.
; Initialize a twenty-four-step sequence using four parallel preset-index tables.
; Each step may update pulse one, pulse two, triangle and noise; zero preset indices leave that voice
; unchanged.
; Four parallel twenty-four-entry preset-index arrays for pulse one, pulse two, triangle and noise.
; Zero means leave that voice unchanged for this step.
; Initialize a sustained pulse preset and alternating timer effect.
; Alternate two pitches, then play two closing presets at distinguished phase counts.
; Initialize two presets with independent table-driven delays.
; Advance the final two-preset sound until the sequence ends.
; Two hold durations and two preset offsets for the closing two-note pulse sequence.
; Copy eight bytes from a preset into both pulse channels.
; Use A as the preset byte count and start at pulse channel one.
; Copy four preset bytes to pulse channel two.
; Copy four preset bytes to the triangle registers.
; Copy four preset bytes to the noise registers.
; Decrease the shared effect delay. If nonzero, discard this helper's caller return so the effect
; update returns immediately; zero resumes the next effect step.
